analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: no executable code, keys, endpoints or protocol behavior changed, so I found no security regression.

Coverage limit: only head text was supplied for docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (lines 445-881). The diff and base side were not, so I could not tell which lines changed. Its prose still matches the T-041 posture. It keeps the HMAC-keyed names, the epoch and binding barriers on SSD owned operations, and authenticated manifest and file reads before any adoption. It also keeps the demand-gated donation writes (`SSDCheckpointDemand.admitsWrite`, lines 502-508 and 670-675), where older coordinators and local serving write unconditionally. That gating is a wear and at-rest-surface control, and it is unchanged in kind. Reviewers of the code PRs should check that the code matches this prose. In particular, the 'record unreadable -> refuse, keep epoch' vs 'record read and gone -> disown' semantics (lines 486-491) are unverified here.

The new docs/design/glm53-flash-native.md is explicitly not qualified. It keeps `glm5_next` out of `EngineV2SupportedModels`, requires cache identity to bind artifact, template and the authenticated scope, and defers to the encryption.md cache-storage protections (lines 16, 81-83). It states that header-only tensor evidence is not payload hashing (lines 30-34) and that the community artifact's identity is a separate gate. It forbids prompts, token IDs, media or tool arguments in telemetry (line 122). Any future code PR that registers GLM must be checked against T-041/A-001 (cache scoping), T-027 and T-012 (artifact and weight integrity), and the MTP/recurrent checkpoint codecs. This PR creates no new attack surface.

docs/developer/build.md and docs/design/README.md contain only cross-references and a build note. They say to use the locked Swift-Jinja pin with no dependency patch, which does not weaken supply-chain integrity. No threat-model update is needed.
